name: Learn the NATO phonetic alphabet
blurb: Alfa to Zulu. Twenty-six words that make spelling anything over a bad phone line unambiguous — genuinely useful, and learnable in an evening.
steps: Learn it in chunks of five letters, saying each aloud rather than reading silently.
Learn the awkward spellings that trip people up: Alfa and Juliett are spelled that way deliberately for non-English speakers.
Practise by spelling out signs, number plates and names you see during the day.
Learn the number pronunciations too: “niner” for nine, “tree” for three.
Have someone read random letters for you to convert, and then the reverse.
Use it for real on the next phone call where you have to spell something.
tips: Speed comes from over-learning. Drill until the word arrives before you think of the letter.
Say it aloud while learning. This is a spoken code, and silent reading trains the wrong thing.
proof: You spell any word aloud in the alphabet at conversational speed, with no hesitation.
